title: ledum palustre subsp. decumbens
intro: Ledum palustre subsp. decumbens, commonly known as low-growing Labrador tea, is a subspecies of the Ledum palustre plant, which is a low-growing shrub found in boggy areas. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, offering health benefits such as antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory effects, which can aid in treating respiratory issues and wound healing. The therapeutic actions of low-growing Labrador tea include its ability to act as an expectorant, helping to relieve congestion and coughs, as well as its antioxidant properties, which can help to protect against cell damage. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenes, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential therapeutic uses.
